title: Demystifying Attention Mechanisms
excerpt: A deep dive into the intuition and math behind attention in neural networks.
body:
Attention is the idea that made modern deep learning click. Transformers, large language models and most state-of-the-art vision models are built on it, yet the core mechanism fits on a napkin. In this post we'll build it up from scratch.

## Attention as a soft lookup table

Imagine a dictionary that maps *keys* to *values*. A normal lookup returns the value whose key exactly matches your query. Attention does something gentler: it compares your **query** with *every* key, turns the similarity scores into weights, and returns a weighted average of all the values.

> Attention is a differentiable dictionary lookup: every key contributes, in proportion to how well it matches the query.

## Scaled dot-product attention

With queries `Q`, keys `K` and values `V` stacked as matrices, the whole operation is a single line:

$$ Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ) V $$

The division by `√d_k` keeps the dot products from growing with the dimension, which would otherwise push the softmax into regions with vanishing gradients.

```
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def attention(q, k, v, mask=None):
    d_k = q.size(-1)
    scores = q @ k.transpose(-2, -1) / d_k ** 0.5
    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, float("-inf"))
    weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    return weights @ v, weights
```

## Why multiple heads?

A single attention head produces one weighted average, so it can only focus on one kind of relationship at a time. Multi-head attention runs several heads in parallel on lower-dimensional projections, letting the model attend to syntax, position and meaning simultaneously, then concatenates the results.

## The cost of looking everywhere

Comparing every query with every key costs `O(n²)` in sequence length. That is fine for a paragraph and painful for a book or a high-resolution image, which is why so much current research, including my own, focuses on **sparse and efficient attention**.

## Takeaways

- Attention is a weighted average whose weights come from query-key similarity.
- Scaling by √dₖ keeps training stable.
- Multiple heads capture different relationships in parallel.
- Quadratic cost is the main bottleneck for long inputs.
